skill.name: write-contract
skill.description: Write production-quality GenLayer intelligent contracts with pinned runners, consensus-safe validation, durable storage, resilient LLM handling, and cross-contract patterns.
skill.summary: Build GenLayer contracts that handle consensus, storage, external data, errors, and contract interactions reliably.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Three eval-related findings are confirmed because the skill recommends executing LLM-generated expressions, despite restricted builtins and a sandbox. The remaining static findings are false positives caused by markdown backticks, headings, prose, or legitimate web and RPC guidance.

remediation.issue: The rule-checking example evaluates LLM-generated expressions.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval with a small allowlisted expression parser, or enforce a separately hardened sandbox with strict resource limits and tests for escape attempts.

remediation.issue: The cross-chain example accepts an RPC URL as a function argument.
remediation.suggestion: Use an allowlist of trusted RPC hosts, validate URL schemes, and document that requests must not include credentials or private data.

remediation.issue: The skill includes operational commands such as contract linting.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples scoped to trusted project files and require user confirmation before running commands or modifying files.

content.value_statement: GenLayer contracts must survive validator disagreement, changing external data, storage constraints, and unpredictable LLM responses. This skill provides practical patterns for consensus-safe contract design, error handling, storage, and cross-contract workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explain when GenLayer consensus is appropriate for a contract workflow.
Select strict equality or comparative validation for nondeterministic operations.
Design persistent storage with GenLayer types such as TreeMap and DynArray.
Handle LLM, external API, and transient errors with explicit error categories.
Show patterns for web requests, cross-contract calls, factories, and cross-chain RPC.
Recommend pinned GenVM runner dependencies and a contract testing sequence.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a deployed contract or audited implementation.
It cannot verify current GenLayer APIs, runner hashes, network behavior, or RPC availability.
External web data can change, fail, or disagree between validator requests.
Generated contracts still require linting, tests, review, and deployment-specific security analysis.

use_cases.title: Build a dispute contract
use_cases.description: Define evidence inputs, validator comparison, settlement effects, and an appeal path for an on-chain dispute workflow.

use_cases.title: Review consensus logic
use_cases.description: Assess whether a proposed LLM or web workflow independently verifies the leader result and compares the fields that affect state.

use_cases.title: Plan contract storage
use_cases.description: Translate ordinary Python collections and numeric values into persistent GenLayer types with upgrade-aware layout rules.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a GenLayer boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this feature: [describe feature]. State whether GenLayer consensus is necessary. Separate frontend, backend, contract, and external-source responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Select a validation principle
prompt_templates.prompt: Design validation for this operation: [describe operation]. Identify nondeterministic inputs, stable decision fields, comparison rules, failure behavior, and cases where strict equality is unsafe.

prompt_templates.title: Map contract storage
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this state model into GenLayer storage: [describe fields]. Recommend types, initialization, numeric representation, collection indexes, and upgrade-safe field ordering.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a contract workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this contract design: [paste design]. Produce a threat model covering validator disagreement, leader manipulation, external data, LLM errors, cross-contract calls, RPC endpoints, and resource limits. Give prioritized fixes and tests.

output_examples.input: A contract classifies uploaded evidence and releases escrow when validators agree.
output_examples.output: Use comparative validation. Validators should independently inspect the same evidence, compare the settlement decision and normalized fields, reject malformed or conflicting results, and expose an appeal path.

output_examples.input: A contract stores user balances, item records, and a variable-length activity list.
output: Use sized integer types for balances and avoid native floating point for money.
Use TreeMap for keyed records and DynArray for ordered activity entries.
Append new storage fields at the end when preserving upgrade compatibility.

best_practices: Pin a concrete runner hash and verify the dependency header before returning contract code.
Compare substantive decision fields or independently derive outcomes from the same source data.
Classify errors explicitly and force disagreement when an LLM produces an invalid result.
anti_patterns: Do not use strict equality for nondeterministic LLM calls or changing web pages.
Do not let validators check only output shape, labels, or confidence ranges.
Do not store native Python lists, dictionaries, or unscaled floating-point money values.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates design guidance and contract examples for GenLayer intelligent contracts. It does not deploy or audit a finished contract.

faq.question: When should I use GenLayer?
faq.answer: Use it when validator agreement is needed for subjective, external, or AI-mediated decisions that change on-chain state.

faq.question: When should I avoid GenLayer?
faq.answer: Prefer a normal backend or deterministic contract when no validator-verifiable judgment is required.

faq.question: How should validators check LLM results?
faq.answer: Rerun the task, independently derive the result, or verify it against the same source and explicit criteria.

faq.question: How should I handle external APIs?
faq.answer: Extract stable fields, classify failures, validate endpoints, and compare derived outcomes instead of unstable timestamps or counts.

faq.question: Is the generated contract production-ready?
faq.answer: No. Run the project linter, direct tests, integration tests, security review, and deployment-specific checks before production use.
